notes.text: For more than 4, bake in two rounds of two pans, so the fries stay spread out.

move.title: Even sticks, hot oven
move.body: Julienne means cutting food into thin, even sticks. Today you'll cut potatoes into shoestrings, then bake them in a hot oven until they're golden and crisp, with no frying.

why.title: Make a flat side first
why.body: A potato is round, and round things roll under a knife. Slice a thin piece off one side and set the potato on that flat side. Now it can't wobble. Almost every vegetable you cut from now on starts this way.

why.title: Same size, same time
why.body: In the oven, thin sticks brown faster than thick ones. If the sizes are mixed, the thin ones burn before the thick ones are done. Even sticks all turn golden at the same moment.

why.title: Why soak them
why.body: Cut potatoes are covered in loose starch, the white cloudy stuff you'll see in the water. Rinsing it off keeps the fries from gluing together, so they crisp up instead.

why.title: Dry fries, spread out
why.body: Water has to steam away before anything can brown. Wet fries, or fries piled on top of each other, steam in their own water and come out soft. Dry them well and give each one its own space on the pan.

wrong.sign: The fries are soft and pale
wrong.fix: They were wet or crowded. Spread them out more and bake a few minutes longer.

wrong.sign: Some fries are burnt and others are still pale
wrong.fix: The sticks were different sizes. Pull out the dark ones and let the rest keep going.

wrong.sign: The fries are stuck to the pan
wrong.fix: Wait a minute after they come out of the oven, then slide the spatula under them. Parchment helps them let go.

quiz.q: Why do the potatoes need to be dry before baking?
choices: Water has to steam away before they can brown
quiz.explain: Wet fries steam instead of browning. Dry ones get crisp.

quiz.q: Why cut all the sticks the same size?
choices: So they all finish baking at the same time
So they fit in the bowl
quiz.explain: Same size means same cooking time, so none burn and none stay raw.

steps.text: Put one oven rack just above the middle and one just below it. Heat the oven to 425°F. Line 2 sheet pans with parchment.
Lay a potato on the cutting board. Slice a thin piece off one long side, and turn the potato so it sits on that flat side.
steps.tip: Hold the food with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front. The flat of the knife slides along your knuckles.

steps.text: Slice the potato the long way into planks about as thick as a pencil.
steps.tip: Keep the knife straight up and down so the planks come out even.

steps.text: Stack 2 or 3 planks and julienne them: slice the stack the long way into sticks as wide as they are thick. Drop the sticks into the big bowl. Cut the rest of the potatoes the same way.
steps.look: Square-ended sticks that are all about the same size.

steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold water and let them soak.
steps.look: The water turns cloudy as the starch comes off.

steps.text: Pour off the water, and dry the bowl. Spread the potatoes on a kitchen towel and pat them as dry as you can. Put them back in the dry bowl.
steps.tip: Take your time here. Dry fries are crisp fries.

steps.text: Add the oil, {qty:salt} salt, and the garlic powder and smoked paprika if you're using them. Toss with your hands until every stick is shiny.
Spread the fries over the two pans in one layer, with a little space around each one.
steps.tip: If they're piled up, they'll steam. Use another pan if you need to.

steps.text: With oven mitts on, take out one pan at a time. Turn the fries over with the spatula, then put the pans back on the opposite racks.
steps.tip: Swapping racks helps both pans brown the same.

steps.text: Bake until golden brown and crisp.
steps.look: Golden brown, with crisp, darker ends.

steps.text: Use oven mitts to take out the pans. Let the fries cool for a couple of minutes, then serve with ketchup if you like.
